bands.why: A reasonable player wins most first levels (0.73 measured), but not every one.
The hardest level row is hard (0.14 measured), yet still winnable.
Random placement mostly loses (0.22 measured): choosing where to clear must matter from the first level.
A level lasts a couple of minutes (median 20 placements), never seconds.
An endless run outlasts a level (median 26 placements measured) and still ends.
A reasonable endless run scores more than a level (median 185 measured).
Endless runs are where aimed beams matter most (2.35 beam hits per run measured).

notes: First run (4 level rows on the 0..100 scale sampled at their lower bounds 0/25/50/75, 100 seeds): greedy won 0.73/0.56/0.39/0.04, a cliff at the last row. Changed one knob: the last row's march 3 -> 4 placements; greedy now wins 0.73/0.56/0.39/0.14, a drop of at least 0.17 per row. Random wins 0.22 of the easiest level and mostly loses by filling the board; the lookahead bot wins every level-2 run. The first placement always fires a beam that defeats a monster (prepared opening). The endless run (difficulty 100) is its own block, never a step of the curve: runs last a median 26 placements, score a median 185 and end about half by a full board. Checked the brief's 'march every placement' with 6-row lanes: greedy won 0.16/0/0/0, so marches stay a per-row knob until the owner decides.
